properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 30 at 12:46AM MST until July 30 at 7:45AM MST by NWS Flagstaff AZ
properties.description:
FFWFGZ

The National Weather Service in Flagstaff has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Paria River in...
Coconino County in north central Arizona...

* Until 745 AM MST /845 AM MDT/ Tonight.

* At 1246 AM MST /146 AM MDT/, upstream river gauges in Utah
indicated a Flash Flood wave moving down the Paria River and into
Arizona. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Gauge indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Paria River.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lees Ferry.

This includes the Colorado River near mile marker 0.

This includes the following recreation areas and campgrounds...
Lees Ferry Camp Site.

This includes the following creeks, washes and rivers...
Colorado River and Paria River.
properties.instruction:
Get out of the Paria River slot canyon! Flood waters will flow down
the Paria River, reaching the confluence with the Colorado River at
Lees Ferry around 7-8 AM MST.

CMAMlongtext: National Weather Service: A FLASH FLOOD WARNING is in effect for this area until 7:45 AM MST. This is a dangerous and life-threatening situation. Do not attempt to travel unless you are fleeing an area subject to flooding or under an evacuation order.

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued July 30 at 3:30AM EDT until July 30 at 4:15AM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
SMWMHX

The National Weather Service in Newport has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
S of Cape Lookout NC to Surf City NC out to 20 NM...
S of Ocracoke Inlet NC to Cape Lookout NC out to 20 NM...
Waters from Cape Lookout  to Surf City NC from 20 to 60 NM...
Waters from Ocracoke Inlet to Cape Lookout NC from 20 to 60 NM...

* Until 415 AM EDT.

* At 329 AM EDT, severe thunderstorms capable of producing
waterspouts were located along a line extending from 24 nm
southwest of Big Ten Fathom to 11 nm south of 14 Buoy to near Atlas
Tanker, moving southeast at 15 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can easily overturn boats and create locally
hazardous seas. Small craft could be damaged in briefly
higher winds and suddenly higher waves.

* Severe thunderstorms will remain over mainly open waters.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Thunderstorms can produce sudden waterspouts. Waterspouts can easily
overturn boats and create locally hazardous seas. Seek safe harbor
immediately.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 8:07PM MDT until July 30 at 2:00AM MDT by NWS Salt Lake City UT
properties.description:
FFWSLC

The National Weather Service in Salt Lake City has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Central Kane County in southern Utah...

* Until 200 AM MDT.

* At 807 PM MDT, trained weather spotters reported flash flooding in
Lick Wash downstream through Buckskin Gulch. Between 1 and 1.5
inches of rain have fallen upstream with a very large flood wave
overflowing its banks while moving south past the intersection
with US-89 heading towards Buckskin Gulch. Expect the very large
flood wave to take roughly 5 hours to reach the confluence with
the Paria River on the Utah side just north of the Arizona border.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding.

SOURCE...Trained spotters reported.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of creeks, streams,
slot canyons, and normally dry washes.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Lick Wash Slot Canyon down to Buckskin Gulch in Central Kane County
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Move to higher ground now. Act quickly to protect your life.

Be especially cautious at night when it is harder to recognize the
dangers of flooding.

Remain alert for flooding even in locations not receiving rain. Dry
washes, streams, and rivers can become raging killer currents in a
matter of minutes, even from distant rainfall.

Flooding is actively occurring. It is important to know where you
are relative to streams, rivers, or creeks which can become killers
in heavy rains. Campers and hikers should avoid streams or creeks.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued July 29 at 8:29PM CDT by NWS Corpus Christi TX
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Three Rivers affecting Live Oak County.

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden, Three Rivers...Major
flooding is forecast.

- Forecast...The river is expected to fall to 17.8 feet Monday
evening.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 22.0
feet on 07/01/1942.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Caution is urged when walking near riverbanks.

Even 6 inches of fast-moving flood water can knock you off your feet
and a depth of 2 feet will float your car. Never try to walk, swim,
or drive through such swift water. If you come upon flood waters,
stop, turn around and go another way.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.
